Whitepaper · from the repository

Practice that teaches people and trains simulated robots

SmartCiti.X Holodeck is a browser and headset training platform. The same practice has a teaching job and a data job: it teaches people to work safely around robots, and only when an adult learner opts in does it become demonstration data, on that learner's device, for simulated robots. Every figure below names the committed repository file it comes from. The robots are simulated; no hardware result is claimed.

The problem

The dangerous moments need practice without the danger

People who work beside robots — apprentices, robot technicians, the specialists who collect and review demonstrations — need to practise the dangerous moments without the danger. The teams building robot and software-agent behaviour need demonstrations with the safety rules built in, gathered with consent. Today these are two separate efforts. This platform makes them one practice, with the teaching job first.

  • Who it is for: apprentices and robot technicians who need robot-safety training; AI-training specialists who collect and review demonstrations; robotics and software-agent teams who want a gym with safety rules built in. No union, employer or robot maker is named as a partner, because there is none. docs/robotics-programme.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Every demonstration measured so far is synthetic or a labelled scripted stand-in; a measured study with real, opted-in adults is planned, not built. docs/consoles/ROBOTRAIN-5.md docs/consoles/COLEARN.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md

What the platform does

A training catalogue, a robot gym and a safety governor

A learner walks a city, opens a station and performs a scored procedure on a flat screen or in a headset. Robot stations sit inside the same catalogue. Behind them, a gym of simulated scenarios trains and scores robot policies, and a governor stands between every software agent and every simulated robot.

  • 742 stations in 61 programmes, scored by the platform's own content evaluation: mean 95.8 out of 100, 612 at 95 or more. docs/investor/platform-summary.json docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Stations are taught against a registry of 513 standards, codes and programmes, named by title and never quoted. docs/investor/platform-summary.json
  • The learning loop runs in the app: demonstrate, consent, train, evaluate, and the robot demonstrates back (5 of 5 steps live). docs/robotics-programme.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • A safety governor between software agents and simulated robots: e-stop first, 11 refusal reasons including a per-agent rate limit and a learned anomaly check that can only add a refusal, and a hash-chained audit log. docs/consoles/VBRIDGE.md docs/consoles/GOVERNOR-2.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Learner data stays in the browser it was made in; nothing leaves the device without the learner's explicit action. WebXR/privacy.html

The Omega Hive

Software agents that manage the robots, and say they are software

The Omega Hive is the collective of software agents that coordinates every simulated robot job. Each agent has a persona, a style of speech, an on-device voice that is off until the learner turns it on, and a body that stands at the robot site it manages. The agents bid for jobs, hand them over, and ask the learner before anything that names the physical path. They are not a language model: every line is generated on the device from the agent's persona and the event's own data.

  • 0.950accuracy naming the speaking agent on 5,686 held-out lines; chance 0.143 docs/consoles/OMEGA-HIVE.md
  • 13.715 → 0.034mean steps from a job's announcement to its award: one dispatcher, then the hive docs/consoles/OMEGA-HIVE.md
  • 10 of 10approval requests asked of the learner wherever the physical path is named docs/consoles/OMEGA-HIVE.md docs/wiki/Roadmap-and-Changelog.md
  • The agents talk to each other at handoffs: 0 → 258 agent-to-agent exchanges in a seeded day, with 516 of 516 lines whose facts come from the award, the bid or the chain, and the governor still checking 161 of 161 jobs. docs/consoles/HIVE-4.md
  • They remember their own day from the hive's chain (36 of 36 memory references grounded), and a regressor recovers their traits from text on held-out personas: warmth 0.959, formality 0.832, verbosity 0.977, caution 0.799. docs/consoles/HIVE-4.md
  • “Supervise every job” on a seeded day: with no setting, 150 of 155 dispatches ran under the standing approval; with it on, dispatches without the learner's approval: 0 of 116. docs/consoles/HIVE-IN-WORLD.md
  • The hive operations room: 0 → 8 of 8 screens painted from the hive's own data, and 7 of 7 agents at their consoles. docs/consoles/HIVE-5.md
  • 862 of 862 mood changes in 5 seeded days, each traced to an event of the hive’s own, with 0 of 1,076 safety lines carrying a mood phrase and a morning briefing of 35 of 35 grounded lines docs/consoles/HIVE-6.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Moods reach the operations room and the console link (merged into the integration head): each figure’s glow pulses with its agent’s mood, adding no mesh (1680 of 1680 checks equal the hive’s own mood; the combined room in the built page measures 46 meshes and 5,586 triangles on high and 85 and 4,394 on balanced), and the live link carries moods, their causes and the briefing captions (1435 of 1435). docs/consoles/HIVE-7.md docs/wiki/Roadmap-and-Changelog.md

Every agent avatar is labelled “software agent” and is visibly distinct from people. Voices are on-device only; captions always show; nothing listens. Virtuals Protocol appears only as a planned technology; nothing from it is installed, bundled or called. docs/omega-hive.md

Robotics buildings and scenes

Six robot sites, inside and out

Each robot site has a building of its own, seen from the street, and a walk-in room behind its door where the station pads and the agents' spots are reached on foot. Everything is procedural — geometry from code, textures drawn on a canvas — and generic by kind: no real building's interior, no logo.

The agents' bodies

A figure that is plainly a machine, and plainly listening to its own words

On the desktop high tier each agent is a skinned software-agent figure — never a skin tone — whose posture follows its personality, whose mouth follows the words it speaks and whose hands answer the hive's own events. The phone tier and the balanced tier keep a lighter figure, so their budgets never change.

  • Triangles per figure on the desktop high tier: 1,012 → 2,693 on average against a budget of 3,000; draw calls per figure while silent 9 → 3; distinct silhouettes among the 21 pairs of agents 18 of 21 → 21 of 21. docs/consoles/AVATARS-HD.md
  • The real voice controller now forwards each word boundary to the figure (0 → 20 in the checker), and the talk light waits for the voice to start: 11 of 11 spoken lines, against 0 of 11 without the wait. docs/consoles/AVATARS-HD-2.md
  • A crowd level for the operations room: 496–524 triangles a figure (≤ 540); seven figures and the room measure 46 meshes and 5,586 triangles against 6,000; walks crossing a console stay at 0 of 214. docs/consoles/AVATARS-HD-3.md
  • The mouth at a low frame rate: word boundaries stamped with their own time, 0 of 20 → 20 of 20 within 1 ms at 1 Hz frames. docs/consoles/AVATARS-HD-3.md
  • The 34 game characters each speak their own knowledge-pack lines in their own on-device voice: 136 of 136 spoken lines verbatim, and a network voice chosen 0 times. docs/consoles/VOICES.md
  • The console nearest the learner stands at the room level in the operations room: 46 meshes and 5,992 triangles on high against a budget of 120 and 6,000, inside it in 480 of 480 steps; the hive’s moods move the figure’s posture inside the existing ranges, the stop hand unchanged, and with no mood events the pose is byte-identical to before. In the robot rooms with the high-detail robots, the rooms inside the budget go from 3 of 6 to 6 of 6, with 1 agent held back (merged into the integration head). docs/consoles/AVATARS-HD-4.md docs/wiki/Roadmap-and-Changelog.md

Every word-boundary figure comes from a stubbed speech engine; the agents' mouths against a real on-device voice are planned. docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md

Robot learning, measured

Held-out seeds, declared in advance, reported as they came out

Every robot-learning result here comes from the simulator, seeded runs and scripted or synthetic demonstrations. Each retest was declared before its held-out seeds were run, and results that did not beat the plain rule are reported as they are.

  • The safety governor blocked 200 of 200 seeded unsafe agent jobs, each for the intended reason, and wrongly blocked 0 of 200 safe jobs. docs/consoles/VBRIDGE.md
  • Its learned check caught 66 of 100 rule-legal anomalous jobs that the rules alone passed, with 0 of 200 held-out safe jobs wrongly refused. docs/consoles/GOVERNOR-2.md
  • On the hard fleet-routing variant, the gap to the scripted expert went from 0.583 to 0.017 after 5 rounds of corrections with features that read the other robots; the expert's labels are not a person's. docs/evals/colearn.json docs/wiki/Roadmap-and-Changelog.md
  • A reactive agent that waits, then sidesteps, passes 55 of 60 fresh held-out seeds where the earlier one passed 26 of 60 — no search, no planner, no learning. On the same seeds a clone given no planner output ends a gap of 0.683, and a reward for steps still trails the plain rule filter (0.517 against 0.650). docs/consoles/ROBOTRAIN-8.md
  • The best text-reading software agent passes 11.5% of 721 stations, against 100% for a scripted expert that sees the targets. docs/perf/agent-baselines.json docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Labelled synthetic datasets ship with a dataset card in the LeRobot-style and RLDS-style layouts, licence CC0-1.0. docs/robot-datasets.md

Robots compete

Model against model, declared first and run once

An arena runs the platform's model families on the same scenarios and held-out seeds through the governor, with intervals. The Omega Claw's software agents declare each comparison, run it once, audit it, and promote a model or refuse it with a reason. A model that did not beat the clone is reported as measured.

  • 8 × 12 model families on scenarios (9 gym scenarios, 3 of them hard variants, and 3 robot stations) docs/evals/arena.json docs/wiki/Robot-Arena.md
  • 179,248 simulated steps in 4,260 episodes, every one checked by the governor, with 0 dispatches to a physical robot docs/evals/arena.json docs/wiki/Robot-Arena.md
  • −0.093 the small language-conditioned model against the behaviour clone on held-out seeds (interval −0.139 to −0.047): it did not beat it docs/evals/arena.json docs/wiki/Robot-Arena.md
  • 351 episodes in the trainable set, all synthetic, with 0 leakage between splits docs/consoles/ROBO-ARENA.md docs/wiki/Robot-Arena.md
  • The arena’s retest was declared first and run once on fresh held-out seeds with the small model given one hidden layer: it is better than before by 0.133 on the declared gaps (interval 0.028 to 0.235) and still not ahead of the clone (−0.067, interval −0.152 to 0.018, so no difference is claimed); the cobot station went from 0 of 10 to 10 of 10; the station tasks are in the dataset (90 episodes, leakage 0, all synthetic); and a button exports a learner’s own consented takes, 0 when signed out and 2 of 2 for an opted-in adult (merged into the integration head). docs/consoles/ARENA-2.md docs/wiki/Roadmap-and-Changelog.md
  • 45 declared comparisons (9 gym scenarios by 5 challengers), each run once on the held-out seeds 7121 –7180 docs/evals/claw.json docs/wiki/Omega-Claw.md
  • 0 models promoted: no challenger beat the incumbent clone with a clear interval and no broken rule docs/evals/claw.json docs/wiki/Omega-Claw.md
  • 3 of 3 refusal kinds exercised on purpose (an undeclared comparison, a reused held-out seed, a model whose run broke a rule) docs/evals/claw.json docs/wiki/Omega-Claw.md
  • 960 simulated minutes the persistent world ran, with 163 jobs completed and 0 dispatches to a physical robot docs/evals/claw.json docs/wiki/Omega-Claw.md
  • The claw’s second protocol was declared after the arena’s declaration and run once on fresh held-out seeds, with the arena’s small model in it this time: 45 comparisons, 4,140 episodes, 155,744 steps checked by the governor and 0 physical dispatches. Promotions: 0. The small model equals the clone where the clone is perfect and is below it on the port gantry, and the persistent world ran 960 simulated minutes with 0 physical dispatches (merged into the integration head). A side-by-side panel lists the learner stations that match each robot scenario, and shows the port gantry as a gap in the programme. docs/consoles/CLAW-2.md docs/wiki/Roadmap-and-Changelog.md

The Strands harness

A Python harness on the strands-robots interface, simulated only

This project's own Python harness speaks the interface of the open strands-robots library: a tool that wraps a robot, and policies that return actions for an observation and an instruction. The robot is always simulated, every step goes through the safety governor, and no real robot moves. It is not affiliated with that library's authors.

  • 4 robot types a simulated tool maps to an arena scenario (an arm for pick-and-place, a cobot, an AMR carrier, a gantry); a request for real hardware is refused with the governor’s reason docs/evals/strands-declared.json docs/wiki/Strands-Robots-Harness.md
  • 6 policies runnable through the policy interface, 13 weight files (154 KB) exported from the arena’s models tools/ra_export_weights.mjs docs/wiki/Strands-Robots-Harness.md
  • 0 physical dispatches; the bridge also blocks and counts any network call tools/ra_bridge.mjs docs/wiki/Strands-Robots-Harness.md
  • The Strands harness’s one declared held-out comparison ran once through the arena’s committed range: 2,160 episodes, 97,289 steps checked by the governor, 0 physical dispatches, 0 network calls; the learned policies' intervals overlap, so none is ranked above another, and the scripted expert is the upper bound (merged into the integration head). docs/consoles/STRANDS.md docs/wiki/Roadmap-and-Changelog.md
  • No such package. The sample that was asked for imports strands_harness. That package is not part of the library and is not on its package index, so this project provides its own create_harness, named as its own. docs/consoles/STRANDS.md docs/wiki/Strands-Robots-Harness.md
  • Simulated only. No real robot is driven, no port or camera is opened, no hosted model is called and no credential is read. How the same code would connect to real hardware is described, not run. docs/consoles/STRANDS.md docs/wiki/Strands-Robots-Harness.md

The ecosystem

Where the platform meets its sibling repositories

SmartCiti.X and Cognition.X are sibling repositories under the same organisation. They were read at a named commit, read-only: the seams are written down, and nothing is wired into either. No partnership or endorsement is implied, and Router.X has no repository at all.

  • 11 seams documented, each with the shape on both sides and the file that shows it docs/ecosystem.md docs/wiki/Ecosystem.md
  • 214 of 670 union and trade stations mapped to a Cognition.X block by declared rules, 456 unmatched and listed docs/ecosystem/blocks-match.json docs/wiki/Ecosystem.md
  • 24 of 24 adult robotics-programme skills mapped to blocks docs/ecosystem/blocks-match.json docs/wiki/Ecosystem.md
  • 91 blocks in the committed extract (73 KB, attributed, CC BY 4.0) docs/ecosystem/blocks-match.json docs/wiki/Ecosystem.md
  • Documented, mostly not wired. The bus adapter and the blocks bridge are built and checked locally. No learner profile, event or block crosses into either sibling repository, and nothing here changes them. docs/consoles/ECOSYSTEM.md docs/wiki/Ecosystem.md
  • Router.X is absent. No repository exists for it. The interface this repository would expect from it is written down and marked not yet built. docs/consoles/ECOSYSTEM.md docs/wiki/Ecosystem.md

The stack

Static files, a flat bundle, and a gate that runs before anything ships

LayerWhat it isSource
WebXR and three.jsEvery world is a WebXR page rendered with three.js, vendored with its licence, so a page runs on a flat screen, a phone or a headset from static files.WebXR/vendor/three/LICENSE
The flat bundlerOne script inlines each app's ES modules and the shared engine into a distributable HTML file, publishes every app beside the homepage in one flat folder, and lets SmartCiti.X lazy-load its station sims; a gatekeeper checker proves every module calls only what it declares or imports.tools/bundle_webxr.py tools/check_imports.mjs
On-device speechOnly a speech-synthesis voice whose localService is true is ever used; a network voice is never chosen. Voice is off until the learner turns it on, and captions always show.WebXR/shared/oh-voice.js
The checker suite and gateOne command runs every headless checker and reports one line each: the parse and import gatekeepers first, then the rest in a pool that respects the shared machine's load.tools/check_all.mjs
CIThe WebXR checks workflow runs the whole gate on every push and pull request that touches the WebXR apps or the tools, and fails a stale committed bundle. It checks out the full history, so the checks that prove a protocol was declared before its run can see their commits, and installs PyYAML for the checker that reads the workflow files..github/workflows/webxr-checks.yml
Deploy configsThe flat build deploys as static files: a Pages config, an API router, generated header and redirect rules, and a deploy agent that runs build, gate, deploy, verify and rollback, as a dry run by default with credentials only from the environment. The deploy workflow is gated on its secrets being present.docs/deploy-cloudflare.md wrangler.toml
Data formatsTraining records export as CSV, xAPI, Open Badges and a printed transcript; robot episodes export in LeRobot-style and RLDS-style layouts with a dataset card.WebXR/privacy.html docs/robot-datasets.md
Search and share metadataOne generator stamps every page's title, description, canonical link, Open Graph and Twitter tags and JSON-LD, and writes the sitemap — this page included.tools/gen_seo.mjs

The roadmap

What is built, and what is only planned

  • Built A robot gym: 6 simulated scenarios, scripted experts and a behaviour-cloning learner, scored on held-out seeds beside a random floor. docs/robot-training.md docs/consoles/COLEARN.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Built Consent, dataset cards and lineage: a revoke marks dependent policies stale, and the registry moves between devices as a file whose tampering is refused by name. docs/robotics-programme.md docs/robot-datasets.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Built A pilot kit: 30 cohort templates, the instructor console, the consent flow with its draft terms, and a bench protocol that is a method (0 hardware runs). docs/instructor-console.md docs/bench-protocol.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Planned A measured study with real, opted-in adults. The app can train on a learner's own takes, but every demonstration measured so far is synthetic or a labelled scripted stand-in. docs/consoles/COLEARN.md docs/consoles/ROBOTRAIN-5.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Planned A measured study of how learners use the hive: its approval setting, its voices and its labels have not been tried by any person. docs/consoles/HIVE-IN-WORLD.md docs/omega-hive.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Planned A native speaker’s review of the hive’s Spanish, which is machine-assisted. docs/consoles/HIVE-3.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Planned A rated robot run that carries a signal, and a further test of the reward for steps on a new range declared in advance: the fairer try on fresh seeds still trailed the rule filter, the rated pair so far has identical features, and corrections still come from the scripted expert. docs/consoles/ROBOTRAIN-7.md docs/consoles/ROBOTRAIN-8.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Planned The agents’ mouths against a real on-device voice: every word-boundary figure here comes from a stubbed speech engine. docs/consoles/AVATARS-HD.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Planned A headset session on hardware for the teleoperation pad. The loop is proven with a stubbed session. docs/consoles/ROBOTRAIN-2.md docs/consoles/ROBOTRAIN-3.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Planned A bench pilot: one task scored the same way in the Holodeck and on a physical robot, with the gap published. No hardware run has happened. docs/bench-protocol.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md
  • Planned Virtuals Protocol (its Agent Commerce Protocol and GAME framework) as a technology the project plans to use for on-chain agents; nothing from it is installed, bundled or called, and no partnership is stated. docs/virtuals-bridge.md docs/agent-roadmap.md docs/wiki/Executive-Summary.md

The robots are simulated; no hardware result is stated. No partnership, customer or commercial figure appears on this page. Standards are named, never quoted, and nothing here claims compliance. The full evidence table and changelog are in the repository's wiki. docs/wiki/Evidence.md

This page is static: it reads the same without JavaScript. It is generated by tools/gen_whitepaper_page.mjs from the wiki and the committed notes; every figure above is copied from the committed file cited beside it, and tools/check_whitepaper_page.mjs fails if one is not found there.
